_note: Functions whose mutants are NOT a statement about shipped behaviour. The mutation queue ranks by SURVIVOR COUNT, and count is a measure of SIZE, not of value — so without this the list sends the next session to write tests for a synthetic-data generator. #1196 measured this population at 15.4 % of the fleet.
_rules: DEFAULT IS PRODUCTION. An entry is added only after reading the function and confirming it. A wrong exclusion silently deletes real work from the queue, which is the unrecoverable direction; a missing exclusion merely leaves noise in the ranking.
NEVER SILENTLY DROP. tools/mutation-worklist.mjs reports the excluded set and its total beside the ranked list, so the reader sees what was set aside and can disagree with it.

A NAME PATTERN IS NOT EVIDENCE. `sampleHz` matched the /^sample[A-Z]/ heuristic used to FIND candidates and is real production code — it computes a sampling frequency and is called three times in its own file. It is deliberately absent below. Every candidate is read before it is listed.

These are NOT equivalence claims. The mutants may well be killable; they are excluded from the ranked list because killing them would assert something about a fixture generator or a self-check, not about analysis a user sees. They stay in the denominator.

cpapdex-dsp.js.why: The DSP's own self-check, exported and run by the gated suite (`CpapDsp.selfTest()`). Its mutants change assertion TEXT and TOLERANCES inside that check — e.g. `ok('near() REJECTS a value just outside the tolerance', !near(10, 10.75, …))`. Killing them means writing tests that assert a self-test's tolerances are correct, i.e. testing the test.
cpapdex-dsp.js.verified: 2026-08-15 — read the function; it is a pass/fail counter over `ok(...)` calls, reachable only as an exported diagnostic.

cpapdex-dsp.js.why: The synthetic-night FIXTURE BUILDER that cpapdex's already-excluded `selfTest` consumes. It sits directly under the file's `SELF-TEST — synthetic session with known truth` header, and all three of its call sites (L1572, L1588, L1589) are inside `selfTest` itself. Its surviving mutants change literals in the generated night — a draft against one asserts `5000 === 5000` — so killing them asserts something about test data, not about analysis a recording takes. Same population as this file's `selfTest` entry and as ecgdex/glucodex `genSynthetic`; it was simply missed. Being exported (L2130) does not make it production: `selfTest` is exported and run by the gated suite and is excluded on the same reasoning.
cpapdex-dsp.js.verified: 2026-08-25 — read the function and every call site. Reported by tepna-99's draft-bank round 2, whose drafts against it were rejected as fixture tautologies. ⚠️ Their report said 'four cpapdex survivors'; that is their count of REJECTED DRAFTS, not of survivors. `mutation-worklist.mjs` measures 19, and 19 is what is recorded here — the number came from the tool, not from the message.

ecgdex-dsp.js.why: Seeded synthetic-ECG generator (`opts.seed`, `scenario:'ambulatory'`). Mutating it changes the FIXTURES a test consumes, not any analysis path a recording takes. The file's own comment at L4027 discusses it as the source of test input.
ecgdex-dsp.js.verified: 2026-08-15 — read the function; no call site on any analysis path inside the DSP.

glucodex-dsp.js.why: Seeded synthetic-CGM generator (`opts.days`, `opts.profile` in {'healthy','predm'}). Produces test corpora, not user data.

motiondex-dsp.js.why: Seeded synthetic accelerometer generator (`opts.hz`, `opts.sec`). Test-fixture source.
